overview.summary: Reopen 0.24 to establish a coherent file-canonical memory corpus before 0.25 changes storage and search technology. The plan first fixes identity, serialization, transaction, and migration invariants; then replaces the append-only tool contract; then delivers fresh bounded context, retrieval/recovery integrity, explicit curation, resource limits, operator visibility, and governance.

sharedDecisions.title: Canonical corpus contract
sharedDecisions.description: S01 defines the file-canonical roles, Markdown schema, stable identity, revision, provenance, topic and locator vocabulary consumed by S02–S12.

sharedDecisions.title: Single revision and mutation authority
sharedDecisions.description: S02 establishes one collection revision, lock scope and canonical commit contract; every observation, mutation, curation and maintenance writer must use it.

sharedDecisions.title: Observation and prompt authority boundary
sharedDecisions.description: Raw observations retain provenance but never gain prompt authority by storage location; only guarded curated-memory changes affect the bounded primary-turn index.

sharedDecisions.title: Stable locator and natural-language query contract
sharedDecisions.description: Results are role-discriminated and use canonical source identity, not derived chunk identity; callers pass natural language and each backend alone owns query encoding.

sharedDecisions.title: Fresh bounded primary-turn context
sharedDecisions.description: S06 must deliver the current bounded index and collection revision through existing provider prompt strategies without weakening provider base prompts or leaking personal memory to background scopes.

sharedDecisions.title: Fixed memory safety ceilings
sharedDecisions.description: Canonical Markdown sources are accepted through 64 MiB inclusive; dated observation partitions through 8 MiB inclusive and reject overflow without trimming; each recursive request processes at most 1,000 regular files and 64 MiB aggregate and returns the best 50 ranked results; migration processes at most 256 parsed records per in-memory batch and reports at most 100 diagnostics within 64 KiB UTF-8; aggregate observation usage warns at or above 64 MiB without blocking writes or deleting records. These safety ceilings are constants, not new configuration knobs.

sharedDecisions.title: On-demand system action seam
sharedDecisions.description: S09 adds one small host-callback system-action registration to the existing scheduling run-now service. System actions share overlap protection and read-only list/show/operator visibility but are excluded from timer scheduling, automatic retries and YAML mutation; their IDs are reserved, so a colliding configured job fails validation before scheduling or publication. S11 presents their typed lifecycle without a second administration surface.

sharedDecisions.title: Release boundary and simplicity
sharedDecisions.description: 0.24 owns personal-memory semantics and on-demand curation; 0.25 owns database/hybrid search and QMD deprecation; the following milestone removes QMD; 0.27 owns autonomous stewardship and guarded wiki/KG write semantics, with no new 0.24 package, database, daemon or scheduler.

sharedDecisions.title: Stopped-runtime edit reconciliation
sharedDecisions.description: S01 and S02 define externally edited corpus detection and revision semantics; S03 and S08 reconcile supported stopped-runtime edits before healthy prompt, search or status use; S11 and S12 expose and document recovery.

bindingConstraints.verbatim: No canonical content may exist only in a derived database.
All operations use one validation/mutation authority and the existing shared workspace lock and atomic-write discipline.

No autonomous background curation is introduced in 0.24; explicit execution registers one host callback as a system action on the existing run-now surface. Its descriptor is read-only through scheduling configuration surfaces, and it is excluded from timers, automatic retries, and YAML mutation while sharing overlap protection and list/show visibility.
The default loaded representation is capped at both 150 rendered lines and `memory.max_bytes` (default 32 KiB), whichever is reached first.
Search callers pass plain natural language; each backend exclusively owns its query encoding/escaping.

A dated observation partition is accepted through 8 MiB inclusive; a limit-plus-one append is rejected instead of trimming prior observations. Recursive traversal processes at most 1,000 regular files and 64 MiB aggregate per request, and search returns the best 50 results after ranking every admitted candidate, with explicit degradation signals when a processing ceiling is reached.
Do not add a new package, database, daemon, scheduler, approval framework, or speculative provider abstraction for this work.
0.27 retains guarded wiki/KG knowledge-write policy and semantics; 0.24 memory mutation tools do not write wiki/KG or broaden their existing write contracts.
Host OS/runtime user/filesystem are trusted. Plausible crashes, cooperating concurrency, untrusted model/tool content, and normal resource limits are in scope.

stories.name: Canonical memory model
stories.scope: Establish the canonical memory roles, stable entry and collection identity, revisions, provenance, topics, locators and deterministic Markdown round trips while preserving file authority and the wiki/KG boundary.
stories.notes: Justified enabler: later slices cannot safely invent independent identity, serialization or corpus semantics.

stories.name: Atomic memory corpus
stories.scope: Provide bounded corpus snapshots and one shared revision, serialization and all-or-nothing canonical mutation authority for cooperating memory, curation and maintenance operations.
stories.notes: Justified enabler: all later writers must share one CAS and canonical commit contract.

stories.name: Lossless memory migration
stories.scope: Upgrade existing recognized and opaque workspace memory, archive and learnings into their canonical roles idempotently, with recoverable prior state and explicit reporting before derived indexing starts.
stories.notes: The migration is the only 0.24 meaning/format transition; 0.25 must preserve its identities and semantics.

stories.name: Observation and retrieval tools
stories.scope: Deliver bounded provenance-labelled observation and learning capture plus role-discriminated natural-language search/read results with canonical identities and locators, including journal routing and correct read/write policy identity.
stories.notes: Expand step: replacement capture/retrieval tools exist before the old write tool is contracted.

stories.name: Atomic memory apply
stories.scope: Deliver conflict-safe atomic add, revise, merge and remove changes through memory_apply, distinguish canonical success from index degradation, and retire memory_save across every production caller, tool schema, policy, provider mapping, prompt, recipe and document.
stories.notes: Keep all operation kinds in one spec unless the FIS emits OVERSIZE; splitting by operation would fragment atomic semantics.

stories.name: Fresh bounded turn context
stories.scope: Make the current bounded memory index and collection revision effective on every primary human-facing turn across supported prompt strategies while keeping topic detail on demand and personal memory out of ordinary background scopes.
stories.notes: Provider delivery may use existing lifecycle seams but must preserve provider base prompts and satisfy next-turn freshness.

stories.name: Search and citation convergence
stories.scope: Converge all retrieval consumers on backend-owned natural-language query handling, role-discriminated results with canonical personal-memory or native wiki locators, preserved wiki ranking/provenance, one wiki composition owner and equivalent live/rebuilt identity.
stories.notes: QMD keeps compatibility/fallback behavior only and gains no canonical-memory schema responsibility.

stories.name: Index health and recovery
stories.scope: Expose truthful healthy, degraded, rebuilding and unknown index states; reconcile supported stopped-runtime canonical edits before healthy use; and recover deleted or corrupt derived indexes by validating a fresh replacement before swap while preserving prior safe state on failure.
stories.notes: Deleted-index startup must not become a silently healthy empty index when canonical data exists.

stories.name: On-demand memory curation
stories.scope: Deliver explicit bounded model-proposed semantic curation through the shared mutation authority and the existing run-now surface, report conflicts and outcomes, and prove every threshold, heartbeat and post-job automatic consolidator path remains absent after S05 removes it.
stories.notes: Add one host-callback system-action seam inside the existing scheduling service; it is listable and runnable but cannot be timed, retried automatically, or mutated through scheduling YAML. Autonomous scheduling and policy remain 0.27.

stories.name: Memory resource boundaries
stories.scope: Harden deterministic pruning, exact replay deduplication, configuration validation and archive, topic, wiki, observation and recursive-processing boundaries while exposing aggregate raw usage without automatic deletion.
stories.notes: Exact deduplication includes provenance/source-event identity; equal text alone never authorizes deletion.

stories.name: Operator-visible memory lifecycle
stories.scope: Make existing status, Memory, Knowledge, API, CLI and job surfaces distinguish corpus roles, revisions, prompt/observation budgets, curation lifecycle, index health and repair without adding a separate administration system.
stories.notes: Requires API/template tests and project visual-validation workflow for empty, degraded, rebuilding, conflicted and successful states.

stories.name: Memory governance and cleanup
stories.scope: Remove obsolete memory types and helpers, enforce cheap architectural invariants, reconcile affected ADRs and synchronize architecture, package and user documentation with the implemented 0.24 contract, the complete memory_save migration, and exact QMD/guarded-knowledge later-release boundaries.
stories.notes: If the FIS is mechanically oversized, split cleanup/fitness from ADR/documentation while keeping the same final wave.

riskSummary.mitigation: Pin the canonical format with deterministic round-trip, stable-identity and opaque-preservation tests before consumers build on it.
Fault every validation, write and replacement boundary and prove stale or failed commits leave no partial canonical change.
Run migration twice, preserve legacy bytes/semantics and inject failures before every irreversible transition.
Verify stable locators, provenance, bounds, user scope and provider policy mapping across both MCP schema paths.
Prove mixed-operation CAS atomicity, deletion audit constraints, post-commit index degradation and complete legacy-tool removal.
Use provider-specific second-turn freshness tests and preserve provider base prompts and background-scope isolation.
Run one shared punctuation/locator corpus through every caller and instrument wiki composition count.
Test corrupt/deleted targets and build, validate and pre-swap failures on portable filesystem paths.
Prove proposal-only model access, malformed/timeout no-op, concurrent conflict rejection, recursion prevention and zero automatic dispatch.
Pin existing and new limits in exact-limit/limit-plus-one tests and retain raw observations unless the user deletes them.
Contract-test status/API states and visually validate each new Memory lifecycle state against the design system.
Use public-reference scans, negative fitness fixtures, analyzer/barrel gates and code-backed documentation verification.

executionNotes: Execute P1 and P2 serially. After S05, S06/S07/S08 may run in parallel because they primarily own prompt delivery, retrieval consumers and recovery/health respectively. S09 and S10 may then run in parallel. S11 integrates operator surfaces; S12 performs final cleanup, fitness and documentation convergence. An OVERSIZE signal from S05, S06 or S12 requires plan decomposition before execution.
